question: If \((m-2)x^{|m|-1}+3y=5\) is a linear equation in the two variables \(x\) and \(y\), find the value of \(m\).
solution: The degree of x is 1, so \(|m|-1=1\), giving \(|m|=2\) and \(m=\pm2\). Also, the coefficient of x must satisfy \(m-2\ne0\), so \(m\ne2\). Therefore, \(m=-2\).

reference.question: If \((m-2)x^{|m|-1}+3y=5\) is a linear equation in the two variables \(x\) and \(y\), find the value of \(m\).
reference.solution:
Method 1: Use degree and coefficient conditions

The degree of x is 1, so \(|m|-1=1\), giving \(|m|=2\) and \(m=\pm2\). Also, the coefficient of x must satisfy \(m-2\ne0\), so \(m\ne2\). Therefore, \(m=-2\).
